finding.area: pobox-towns: PO-box and other published points whose ZIP has no centroid (40,348 rows, 374 distinct addresses, 325 ZIPs)
finding.summary:
I checked all 374 distinct published addresses in this group: 349 nominatim_city, 20 nominatim and 5 google. Each point was compared with its named town in four ways: (a) a public Nominatim reverse lookup of the point, (b) a structured Nominatim search for the town's own settlement point (city=, state=, no ZIP), (c) the median of the town's other ZIP centroids in the data, and (d) public GeoNames facts on which town each suspicious PO-box ZIP belongs to. 257 of the 349 city pins sit within 0.5 km of their town's settlement point. 21 keys (1,403 rows) are more than 15 km from their town, up to 694 km: 8 committee keys (1,364 rows) and 13 individual keys (39 rows, 13 donors). Another 9 keys (1,294 rows) are 8–15 km away. Most of those are a POI inside the right city, but one is a parish centroid.

Root cause, reproduced live: engines.city_level sends free text "CITY, ST ZIP, USA" with limit=1. OSM does not know PO-box or unique ZIPs. When the ZIP is unknown, the ', USA' word matches POIs whose names contain 'USA'. Examples: 'Lego San Francisco, Miniland USA' in Carlsbad; 'Murphy USA' fuel stations in Sealy (Austin County), south Austin, Columbia and Augusta; 'Kid City USA' in Longmont; 'Destiny USA Mall' in Syracuse; 'USA Auto Parts' in San Antonio; 'CAE USA' in Tampa. Other hits were counties (Jackson County MS, Jefferson Parish, Napa County) or a road, building or feature named like the town (Crown Point road in Zionsville, a 'Potomac' building in Towson, 'Mill' on Holcomb Valley Rd). The query result's type is never checked.

With no ZIP centroid, _fallback returns the first in-state hit unchecked. The only guard is the state box with a 1-degree margin, and _needs_lookup, prefer_zip_centroids and accepted_coordinates never re-examine these entries. Round-2's 11 cases are exactly the individual keys more than 20 km off. Round 2 missed the 8 committee keys (1,364 rows).

Everything else is clean. The 25 street-level keys are all consistent with their town except one unverifiable home (I did not research it). The 53 published (verified/grounded) employer offices with no-centroid ZIPs are all within about 10 km of their city.

Fix at the source, free (Nominatim only, no Google or OpenAI). Replace the city query with a structured city/state search that returns settlements only. Then re-check once the cached nominatim_city entries whose ZIP has no centroid (at most 634 free lookups, about 12 minutes). This moves 55 keys / 4,840 rows by more than 0.5 km, or only 30 keys / 2,697 rows if points are replaced only when they are more than 8 km off. mechanisms: fec/geocoding/engines.py:104-109 city_level: builds q=f'{city}, {state} {zipcode}, USA' with limit=1 and never checks the result's type or name. When OSM does not know the PO-box or unique ZIP, the ', USA' word matches POIs named '...USA'. I reproduced this on 2026-09-24. 'SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94141, USA' returns Lego San Francisco, Miniland USA in Carlsbad. 'AUSTIN, TX 78711, USA' returns Murphy USA in Sealy. 'BOULDER, CO 80306, USA' returns Kid City USA in Longmont. 'NEW YORK, NY 10150, USA' now returns Destiny USA Mall in Syracuse. 'SAN ANTONIO, TX 78278, USA' returns USA Auto Parts. Otherwise the query returns a county ('JACKSON, MS 39207' gives Jackson County; 'NAPA, CA , USA' gives Napa County; 'JEFFERSON, LA' gives Jefferson Parish) or a road or building named like the town (Crown Point road in Zionsville; a 'Potomac' building in Towson; 'Mill' on Holcomb Valley Rd). The cached coordinates equal these features' coordinates exactly.

fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:675-681 _fallback: when locality.zip_point is None (ZIP without centroid, or blank ZIP), the first city_point hit inside the state box is returned at once as 'nominatim_city'. Nothing checks it against the town. The no-ZIP query runs only when the ZIP query returns nothing or lands outside the state (that path gave Jefferson Parish after 'JEFFERSON, LA 70183, USA' landed in the US Virgin Islands).

fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:576-585 _Locality.city_point: the only guard is _valid_for_state (pipeline.py:135-140). That is the state bounding box plus 1 degree, and every wrong hit here is inside its own state.

fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:214-218 _far_from_zip and 256-265 _street_far_from_zip return False when the ZIP has no centroid. As a result, _needs_lookup (pipeline.py:381-386) never re-looks up these cached entries, prefer_zip_centroids (330-350) skips them because _zip_point is None, and accepted_coordinates (297-319) publishes them after only the state-box check.

fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:588-593 _inside_filed_zip returns True for a ZIP with no centroid, so street-level hits there are unguarded. The 25 such keys in this group are all plausible; the only large distance is the unverifiable Scottsdale 86259 home.
Caveat for any fix: in a structured Nominatim query, state='LA' was read as Los Angeles (it returned the 'Jefferson' quarter in LA, CA). A structured query must pass the full state name.
proposed_fixes: 1 (source, engines.py city_level): replace the free-text 'CITY, ST ZIP, USA' with a structured Nominatim search: city=CITY, state=<full state name from fec.config.geography / us_states.csv>, country=us, with postalcode only when the ZIP has a centroid, and no ', USA' word. Return addresstype. In _Locality.city_point, accept only settlement types (city, town, village, hamlet, suburb, neighbourhood, quarter, borough, municipality), which rejects county, road, building, amenity, tourism and shop. I simulated this on all 256 towns in the group: 255 returned a settlement, and every one agreed within 5 km with an independent town lookup. JAMAICA NY needs the free-text fallback without ', USA'.

2 (source, pipeline.py _fallback): when zip_point is None, publish the town's settlement point. Keep the ZIP-query hit only if it is itself a settlement within 15 km of the no-ZIP settlement point. This matches the documented intent (_zip_replaces_city docstring: 'a PO box sits at the post office, in the named town').

3 (one-time cache re-check, free): in _needs_lookup, return True for source=='nominatim_city' entries whose ZIP is blank or has no centroid and that lack a new 'town_checked' flag. _geocode_todo then writes town_checked=True. Scope: 506 cached nominatim_city entries with a 5-digit no-centroid ZIP plus 128 with a blank ZIP, at most 634 free Nominatim calls (about 12 min at 1 request/s). No Google or OpenAI calls, and no paid cache entries deleted.

Rows changed by 1+2+3, measured against the structured settlement points: 55 keys / 4,840 rows move by more than 0.5 km (4,740 committee rows; 100 individual rows, 23 donors). Of these, 21 keys / 1,403 rows move by more than 15 km and 9 keys / 1,294 rows by 8–15 km. 257 of the 349 keys stay within 0.5 km. A conservative variant replaces a cached point only when the new settlement point is more than 8 km away: 30 keys / 2,697 rows. The other employer, stale and fake-address keys on the same points are corrected too, but none are published.

4 (tests that can fail): unit tests with mocked Nominatim answers (a 'Murphy USA' amenity, 'Jackson County' with addresstype county, a 'Crown Point' road) that must be rejected by city_point. Plus a data test over geocode_cache.json asserting that the 30 keys listed here end within 8 km of their town's settlement point. It fails on today's cache.

5 (spill-over, another area): the same city_level flaw feeds PO boxes whose ZIP does have a centroid. 343 keys / 30,329 rows sit on nominatim_city with a centroid ZIP. _zip_replaces_city keeps a same-town POI whenever it is within the ZIP's street limit; one sample is PO BOX 290820|COLUMBIA|SC|29229 at 19.4 km. Apply the same one-time town_checked re-check there and measure it.

6 (no change needed): the Scottsdale 86259 google point and the other street-level keys. Do not research private homes. Optionally add a town-distance guard (at most 50 km from the settlement point) for street-level hits when the ZIP has no centroid; none of today's 25 keys would trip it.

verdict.area: pobox-towns (verification): points whose filed ZIP has no centroid, 40,348 rows / 374 keys / 325 ZIPs
verdict.measured:
I re-measured everything from the files, read-only. I read the CSVs with keep_default_na=False, built keys with pipeline._contributor_keys, and got 0 mismatches between the cache and the published lat/lng. Group size: 40,348 rows (39,402 COMMITTEE/PAC, 940 INDIVIDUAL, 6 ORGANIZATION), 325 ZIPs, 374 keys (349 nominatim_city, 20 nominatim, 5 google). The individual rows cover 159 donors and 125 ZIPs, and 91.8% are PO boxes. All of this matches the investigator.

I ran my own free public lookups. First, a structured Nominatim settlement search for each of the 256 towns (city=, full state name, featureType=settlement, limit 3). Second, a reverse lookup at zoom 18 for each of the 289 distinct points. Third, Zippopotam/GeoNames for the ZIP-to-town facts. I also re-ran the live free-text queries. 'LITTLE ROCK, AR 72217, USA' returns the North Little Rock boundary with addresstype=town. 'SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94141, USA' returns Lego Miniland in Carlsbad. 'AUSTIN, TX 78711, USA' returns Murphy USA in Sealy. 'JACKSON, MS 39207, USA' returns Jackson County. 'JEFFERSON, LA 70183, USA' returns a road in St Croix, USVI.

Distance from each nominatim_city point to its town's settlement point: 292 keys within 0.5 km, 55 keys (4,844 rows) beyond 0.5 km, and 2 with no settlement match (Jamaica NY, Forest Hills NY). Beyond 8 km: 30 keys / 2,697 rows. Beyond 15 km: 21 keys / 1,403 rows. These last three numbers equal the investigator's.

The reverse lookups show that 8 of those 21 keys sit inside the named city. The 7 Phoenix keys (281 rows) are at 19801 N Tatum Blvd, Desert View, Phoenix 85050. PO BOX 5814 AUSTIN 78763 is at 1414 W Howard Ln, Austin 78728, not Wells Branch as claimed. So only 13 keys / 1,121 rows are more than 15 km away AND outside the named town: 4 committee keys with 1,096 rows (Jackson MS 170, Crown Point 82, Austin 78711 546, Boulder 298) and 9 individual keys with 25 rows and 9 donors (SF ×2, Mill Valley, NY 10150, Austin 78716, Potomac, San Diego 92191, Napa, Albany/Kamas).

With the town-level wrong pins found under 15 km added, the corrected count of pins outside their named town is 15 keys / 2,428 rows: Jefferson LA (662) and Little Rock (645). Richmond 23218 (34 rows) is a borderline 16th. Every raw filing matches the cleaned city/state and ZIP5 (only ZIP+4 is cut off), so the cause is geocoding, not cleaning. The two exceptions are Napa (raw 'NA' / 00000) and the Albany/Kamas filing where the house number was entered as the ZIP.

Employer side: 174 employer_locations rows with a no-centroid ZIP have coordinates (the investigator said 173); 54 of them are published verified/grounded rows (the investigator said 53). All 40 I could compare lie within 6.3 km of their town, so they are clean. AIG (70 PINE ST), BEAR STEARNS (383 MADISON) and TURNING POINT USA (PO BOX 1804 Phoenix) sit on the Destiny USA and N Tatum points, are all uncorroborated, and are filtered out by the PUBLISHABLE_ADDRESS_TRUST filter in the loader (fec/database/loader/addresses.py:45). I found 16 fake AI employer keys on the Sealy and N Tatum points; none are published.

Re-check scope: 506 nominatim_city entries with a no-centroid ZIP plus 128 with a blank ZIP makes 634. But only 349 of them are used by today's contributions and 10 by employer_locations. _needs_lookup only sees keys in the current dataframe, so about 360 free calls would actually run.

Evidence is in scratchpad/cacheaudit/verify-pobox-towns/: keys_v3.csv, v_towns.json, v_rev.json, zippo.json.

The claim '257 of 349 city pins within 0.5 km' contradicts their own '55 keys move >0.5 km'. I measure 292 within 0.5 km, 55 beyond (4,844 rows) and 2 with no settlement match.

It is 19 km from downtown only because 29229 is Northeast Columbia. Moving these to the town center would make them worse.

The re-check cost of 'at most 634 lookups' overstates it. 275 of the 634 are stale keys absent from current data, which _needs_lookup never evaluates. The realistic count is about 360 free calls. Direction confirmed: no Google or OpenAI calls, since _geocode_one has no Google engine.
Minor count differences: 174 no-centroid employer rows with coordinates (they said 173) and 54 published (they said 53). The conclusion (clean) stands.
missed: PO BOX 7839|LITTLE ROCK|AR|72217 (612 rows, COTTON FOR SENATE 7c8bb7975e3f) and PO BOX 7841|LITTLE ROCK|AR|72217 (33 rows, FRENCH HILL FOR ARKANSAS 7bbf8b36ac01) are pinned at 34.769536,-92.2670941, which is 1612 N Main St, North Little Rock, a different city across the river. 72217 has no centroid; GeoNames lists it as Little Rock. I reproduced it live: 'LITTLE ROCK, AR 72217, USA' returns the North Little Rock boundary with addresstype=town. The pin is only 3.3 km from Little Rock's settlement point, so every km threshold misses it, including the proposed 8 km conservative variant. Worse, the proposed settlement-type filter would ACCEPT it because it is a 'town', and fix 2's 'keep the ZIP-query hit if it is a settlement within 15 km' would keep it. The fix needs a name match: the result's name must equal the filed city, allowing City/Town/Village-of and Saint/St.

PO BOX 47|RICHMOND|VA|23218 and PO BOX 818|RICHMOND|VA|23218 (34 rows, MCCLELLAN FOR CONGRESS 085de2ed3060) sit on 'Grifols Biomat USA Plasma Center' in Henrico County, 6.6 km from Richmond city. This is the same '...USA' POI mechanism, just outside the independent city, and falls below the 8 km cut. Minor.

A structured Nominatim search does not strictly filter by state: for HOUSTON|TX the 2nd result was Houston, Missouri. The fix must keep _valid_for_state and take the first in-state, name-matching settlement from limit>1 results, not simply limit=1.

featureType=settlement returned nothing for JAMAICA NY and FOREST HILLS NY. The affected keys are '11425 TWINING LN 11425 TWINING L|JAMAICA|NY|11425' and '11835 QUEENS BLVD 16FLOOR|FOREST HILLS|NY|11376'; the latter currently sits on 'USA Vein Clinic', in the right neighbourhood 1 km from the 11375 centroid. Both current pins are acceptable and would be lost if a re-check that finds nothing overwrites them. The investigator said 255 of 256 towns matched; I get 254 of 256.

Same-name settlements exist within a state in this very group: MAGNOLIA TX (a second one 62 km away), ENTERPRISE AL (173 km), BRENTWOOD TN (3 places), POTOMAC MD (Allegany County, 153 km). Today the first no-ZIP structured result is the right one every time, but dropping the ZIP hint (fix 1) makes that luck. Prefer a name-matching settlement from the ZIP-hinted query when one exists.

Cache-write hazard in fix 3 that the investigator did not mention. _geocode_todo calls put_failed(validated=True), a permanent not_found that is never retried, when the chain returns nothing. For a PO box, _fallback returning None leads to _geocode_international, which rejects US hits. On a NominatimUnavailable error, put_transient blanks lat/lng until the next run. Either way a currently correct town pin is erased. GeoCache.put also has no 'town_checked' parameter, so it needs a signature change.

The re-check also re-runs Census and Nominatim street lookups for the 5 non-PO-box street keys currently on nominatim_city in the group, e.g. '2302 DUXBURY CURCLE|LOS ANGELES|CA|' (at LA city center) and the Forest Hills and Jamaica keys. It is free, but it changes more than the town-point estimate covers.

verdict.fix_risk:
The core diagnosis and mechanism are correct, and I reproduced them live: engines.city_level sends free text 'CITY, ST ZIP, USA' with limit=1 and no type check, and _fallback publishes the first in-state hit when zip_point is None, with no later guard. The fix direction is safe on the stated rules: Nominatim only, no paid Google or OpenAI calls, no paid cache entries deleted, no cleaned address edited, and foreign keys untouched, since _geocode_one routes them to _geocode_foreign first.

It needs these changes before it is safe:
(1) Add a NAME match to the settlement-type filter, otherwise North Little Rock (addresstype=town, 3.3 km) survives both fix 1 and fix 2 for the Little Rock keys (645 rows).
(2) Keep _valid_for_state, and scan several results, because the structured state parameter is not strict (Houston, Missouri appeared for Texas).
(3) Make the one-time re-check write-if-better. Replace the cached point only when a name-matched settlement is found, and never call put_failed or put_transient over an existing working pin. Otherwise the Jamaica and Forest Hills keys, and any town Nominatim cannot type as a settlement, become permanent not_found, and a Nominatim outage blanks rows for a run.
(4) Prefer a ZIP-hinted, name-matching settlement over the no-ZIP one, so that same-name towns (Magnolia TX, Enterprise AL, Brentwood TN, Potomac MD) do not flip to the wrong duplicate.
(5) Do NOT apply fix 5 to centroid-ZIP PO boxes. Those pins are held within their ZIP limit (median 2.4 km from their ZIP centroid), and moving them to downtown would degrade correct in-ZIP post-office pins such as Columbia 29229.
(6) Do not count Albany/Kamas as fixed, and do not count the in-city Phoenix, Austin, Tampa, Columbia, Augusta, Mobile and San Antonio pins as corrections. Moving them to the city center is neutral.

Realistic effect: about 360 free lookups. Truly wrong pins corrected: 15 keys / 2,428 rows (2,403 committee rows, 25 individual rows from 9 donors), plus about 40 in-city keys re-centred. The 8 km conservative variant would leave the Little Rock (645 rows) and Richmond (34 rows) wrong-city pins in place.

mechanisms: fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:246-265 (street_zip_limit_km/_street_far_from_zip): the guard is a circle of radius max(5 km, 2.5× distance to the 3rd-nearest ZIP centroid) around the filed ZIP's centroid. Long or large ZIPs cover the next town or municipality: 33480 (barrier island) 14.8 km, 30326 9.9, 77024 9.6, 89139 13.6, 33412 32.7, 44124 15.1. The confirmed wrong points sit at 0.62-0.99 of the limit, and 4 committee points at only 0.21-0.39.

fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:322-327 (_unchecked_outside_zip) and 353-386 (_needs_lookup): an old nominatim/google entry inside the circle is never queued again, so the current chain (Census first, then _street_in_filed_zip, then engine agreement) never sees 17,363 of the published street points.

fec/geocoding/engines.py:64-77 (nominatim): the structured query sends city=<postal city>+postalcode with limit=1. OSM resolves 'city' to the municipality, so suburbs using a big city's postal name get the same-name street inside that city: unincorporated Clark County as 'Las Vegas' (3 roads all on lat 36.1437-36.1443), the Memorial Villages as 'Houston', Pepper Pike as 'Cleveland', Plymouth as 'Minneapolis', Ladue/Clayton as 'Saint Louis', West Boca as 'Boca Raton'. engines.py:137-140 (_nominatim_request) keeps only lat/lon/country_code, although addressdetails=1 is requested. address.postcode and address.house_number, which would reveal a wrong-ZIP or street-only match, are thrown away.

Street-only matches: Nominatim returns the street's centre when the house number is missing from OSM. The cache stores no precision, so 57 points shared by different house numbers are published as house-level. On long roads they land in another municipality (S Woodland Rd, Valencia Dr, Delmar Blvd).

Direction and suffix variants in the cleaned street (PEACHTREE ST NW vs NE, CRANES PT vs POINTE, '7000 N PHOENIX ST') send the engine to a different segment or street. The old Google entries have no location_type, so approximate hits are labelled 'google' (street-level).

fec/geocoding/pipeline.py:278-294 (_zip_replaces_city) and 670-689 (_fallback): for a street address the ZIP centroid replaces the city point whenever the two are within 50 km. A ZIP typo (2660 S OCEAN BLVD|PALM BEACH|FL|33418) therefore moves the pin to another town (Palm Beach Gardens, about 20 km). PO boxes already get the stricter test (the city must lie outside the ZIP's own limit before the centroid replaces it).

Engine rule for future lookups (fec/geocoding/engines.py nominatim + pipeline._geocode_one). When a 5-digit ZIP is filed, first query street+postalcode+state without city. Then read the address.postcode and address.house_number that addressdetails=1 already returns: a result whose postcode differs from the filed ZIP, or that has no house_number although the street has one, goes into `outside` (so it needs Census agreement or an in-ZIP hit) instead of being accepted on the circle test alone. Store precision ('house'/'street'/'place') in the cache so the DB can tell a street-only match from a house point. This prevents city-clip and street-only pins. Cost: free.

Systematic re-check rule (pipeline._needs_lookup). Queue again the old nominatim/google street entries (no zip_checked, not reviewed) whose distance is more than 0.5× the ZIP limit and whose filed ZIP is not among the 6 centroids nearest the point: 99 keys / 572 rows, covering 22 of the 28 confirmed wrong keys. Run them through the current chain. For Google entries, replace only when Census returns an in-ZIP point more than 1 km away; otherwise keep the paid result and set zip_checked. Cost: about 99 Census calls plus a few hundred Nominatim calls, all free.

Offline cross-check before any re-query (a tools/audits check, fed into the two reviewed lists). Compare each published street point with the other cache entries for the same numbered street and city under other ZIP spellings ('', 'NAN', '.0'). 499 keys have one; 26 disagree by more than 2 km; in 4 the unused paid Google entry is right (fix 2), 2 are probable (3101 S OCEAN DR HOLLYWOOD 33019 59 rows, 6327 EDGEWATER DR ORLANDO 32810 6 rows), 1 is unresolved (4075 LINGLESTOWN RD 17112, 59 rows); the rest keep the published point. verdict.fix_risk:
**Fix 2 (reuse the paid Google points already in the cache): safe.** It costs zero lookups, and I web-checked all the committee and office points against their public locations. Add 3980 BROADWAY ST Boulder (50 rows), 3101 and 2711 S OCEAN DR Hollywood, and probably 4075 LINGLESTOWN RD.

On a Census miss it falls back to the filed ZIP centroid, which is the right town. Remove the Ridge Rd pair: put unresolved keys in a re-check queue without the exclusion.

**Fix 4 (systematic re-check): safe and free, but mostly churn.** About 70 of its 91 keys are correct, and it misses the 4 high-row committee keys.

**Fix 5 (offline cross-checks): safe, and the checks can fail.**

**Fix 3 (engine rule): moderate risk.** In US OSM data address.postcode and house_number are often missing or inferred. Hard-rejecting on them would push many correct results down to ZIP centroids. Store precision as a label instead, and apply the rule to new lookups only.

**Fix 6 (build_employers) as written: unsafe.** It blanks about 45 correct office points, cannot re-geocode the preserved rows, and leaves BARUCH's city point in place.

**Fix 9 (ZIP-typo rule): unsafe.** About 69 keys / 293 rows would move from the right ZIP centroid to the big-city point (Houston, San Antonio, Las Vegas, Cincinnati). Correct the one 33418 row in cleaning instead.

**Fix 8 (cleaning the 4 filings): fine.** It is done in cleaning, which may edit addresses; the geocoder does not. But the state can be derived only for SACKHEIM and from the ZIP inside the street text for AGAM and KREBS; JANIS cannot be recovered.

**Fix 7 (employer offices): fine.** It needs keys in cache-key form (it uses them) and a sourced, not approximate, point for The Spiral.

**Common to all:** none of the fixes touches a foreign key or edits a cleaned address in the geocoder, and none deletes a paid entry. mechanisms: build_employers.py:176 `_cache_rows` uses `address_cache_lookup(cache)` over ALL entries, while resolve's apply.py:30 uses `address_cache_lookup(entries, publishable_only=True)`. In fec/resolve/pipeline/locations.py:148 `_preferred_entry` returns the exact entry whenever it exists (`if exact is not None: return exact`), even when it is closed-book and a canonical sibling is grounded. At line 156, a group with a closed-book sibling at a different address counts as ambiguous and returns None. The publishable lookup filters closed-book entries out first, so apply finds the grounded sibling and geocode.py geocodes it (through the CSV rows), but build_employers publishes the closed-book row (trust corroborated/uncorroborated, dropped by the loader at fec/database/loader/addresses.py:45) or no row at all. This explains the 67.

locations.py:130: `if exact and exact.get('method') in {'manual_invalid','ai_not_found'}: return exact`. An exact ai_not_found beats even a unique grounded or manual canonical sibling, in both lookups. This explains the 4, and earlier forced the hand-made 'twin adjudication' manual rows.

Step 3b, dedup.py:58-72 `_entries_by_address`, groups only entries that already have an address with HIGH/MEDIUM confidence, skips manual_override, and needs an identical normalised address string; `_same_entity` (line 11) then clusters by canonical key or prefix. It is address-first by design. So it can never alias a current name that is ai_not_found, missing, or at a different closed-book address; it never uses EMPLOYER_SYNONYMS (BOFA vs BANK OF AMERICA); and it misses spelling-level address differences ('100 North Tryon Street' vs '100 N Tryon St').

The manual CSV is loaded by exact name (fec/resolve/pipeline/manual_overrides.py `_read_location_groups` / `load_manual_locations`). build_employers.py:120-137 `_abbreviate_trailing_unit` only fires when UNIT_EXTRACT (fec/config/streets.py:14-27) matches keyword-then-one-code at the end of the line. It never matches '10TH FLOOR' (reversed order), 'SEVENTH FLOOR' (spelled), 'SUITE 110 #353' / 'SUITE C 300' (more than one token), or 'SUITE #211' ('#' is not in `[\w\-\/\.]`), and `_UNIT_CODE_RE` (line 131) rejects 'SUITE ONE'. The shared UNIT_RULES (streets.py:140-151) only rewrite a leading keyword, so donor street_2 values like '2ND FLOOR' also stay long-form.

build_employers.py:109-117 `normalize_us_streets` deliberately keeps the unit on the street line ('employer addresses have no street_2'). The loader then inserts employer addresses with street_2=None (fec/database/loader/addresses.py:117 and :209, and employers.py `_employment_address_id` `_akey(..., None, ...)`), while donor rows carry the unit in street_2. None of the fixes needs a paid lookup. Risk by fix:

- **F1 (build uses the publishable lookup first): low risk, but not self-sufficient.** It adds 67 addresses, 65 already pinned. Update/add build tests. Give the 17 employers whose grounded state is not a donor state (WILLIAMS & CONNOLLY stale, BOULEVARD HEALTHCARE uncertain) a review list or a state guard. It saves no paid calls unless collect_employer_lookups also consults the lookup, or the grounded entry is aliased onto the exact key.
- **F2: a policy reversal.** It breaks test_explicit_not_found_is_not_replaced_by_an_alias, so it needs the user's sign-off. The safe version: only a closed-book (provider 'openai') ai_not_found gives way, only to a single grounded or manual sibling, and only when that sibling's state is one of the donors' states.
- **F3:** the acceptance test must compare buildings (normalised street + ZIP family), not the leading number. Agreement with a closed-book address must not be treated as proof the address is current (the MORGAN LEWIS 1701 Market case). Better to review the 13 once and write manual rows than to automate.
- **F4:** delete RADCO and FELSON CO before any generic mapping, because a manual_override overwrites _search entries. Re-key CONGRESS AUTO INSURANCE AGENCY -> CONGRESS AUTO INS by hand. Re-keying PAUL WEISS, PROGRESSIVE, UNITEX and PIERPOINT is fine.
- **F5:** reverses pinned tests (6TH FLOOR, FLOOR 24, SUITE ONE). Keep 'SUITE ONE' unguessed. Donor street_1 edits change about 7 geocode keys. No address meaning changes.
- **F6:** a CSV/loader/geocode-key contract change. The loader tests change. Any consumer that reads only addresses.street_1 for an employer loses the unit (not checked in the dashboard or chatbot repos). The employer geocode keys change too, so ship it with F7.
- **F7:** safe. It only reads existing cache points through accepted_coordinates and moves 32 pins to street level. Re-keying the geocode step to the normalised form causes free but slow Nominatim lookups (about 1 request per second) for new keys.
- **F8:** safe. The user decides row by row, and restoring the rows also avoids paid AI calls.

No fix touches foreign addresses or edits a cleaned donor address through geocoding.

finding.summary:
WHAT IS PUBLISHED. The loader keeps an employer_locations row only if it has a street address and address_trust is verified or grounded (fec/database/loader/addresses.py:45, PUBLISHABLE_ADDRESS_TRUST at fec/resolve/pipeline/locations.py:24). That is 2,799 rows for 2,489 employers.
- Every one of the 2,489 primary rows becomes employers.address_id.
- A non-primary row (310) is used only when select_location picks it for an employee in the same state. 92 of the 310 have no donor in their state, so the loader prunes them.
- Where the published rows come from:
  - 1,466 legacy ai_openai_search entries. These have no source_url, prompt_version or address_type, so nothing can be audited, yet they are labelled "grounded".
  - 339 current v3 sourced primaries plus 303 v3 offices.
  - 20 ai_openai_gpt5_search and 4 ai_xai_search.
  - 635 manual_override.
  - 32 rows with no cache entry at all. build_employers keeps them from old builds, and they keep their old trust label.
- No closed-book ai_openai row is published. build_employers._trust gives "grounded" only to methods ending in _search. The 2 preserved "grounded" rows trace back to legacy search keys.

WEB CHECK. I drew a stratified random sample of 45 rows and extended it for the small strata, then checked each against the company's official site or a reputable directory. I also checked 12 rows from a targeted risk slice: short or acronym names whose office is outside every donor's state. Results by method:
- Legacy search: 14 checked. 9 correct, 3 wrong company (NORWOOD PUBLIC SCHOOL, MPI, AREAS), 2 are the only donor's own home filing address, which I did not research. About 21% wrong company, 36% with some problem.
- v3 primaries: 9 checked. 7 correct, 1 with plausible but unprovable identity, 1 residential (APPROVED FINANCIAL). No wrong company.
- v3 offices: 7 of 7 correct. Only 1 is a retail dealership rather than an office.
- gpt5_search: 10 of the 20 checked. 1 correct, 2 correct but old, 7 wrong (wrong company or wrong street). Every one of the 20 is outside all of its donors' states.
- xai_search: 4 of 4 checked. 3 correct, 1 wrong street (BLUMBERG CAPITAL).
- manual_override: 4 of 4 correct, though one is a mail drop.
- The 32 preserved rows labelled "verified": 8 checked. 5 wrong city or organisation, 1 wrong or old, 1 unverifiable, 1 correct.

State is the strongest signal. In the random sample, 1 of 25 rows whose state matches a donor was wrong (4%). Among the 17 primaries outside every donor's state, 8 were wrong (47%). In the targeted legacy slice, 1 of 12 was wrong, 1 old and 3 unverifiable.
- 740 published primaries (30%) are in a state where none of the employer's donors live. By method: legacy 561, v3 57, gpt5 20, xai 4, manual 88, preserved 10. 554 of them have a single donor.
- Legacy rows have no address_type, so for those 1,466 rows we cannot tell a known headquarters from a namesake.
- Rough totals: about 150–300 wrong-company or wrong-address primaries among the 1,466 legacy rows, about 14 of the 20 gpt5 rows, and about 20 of the 32 preserved rows. That is roughly 7–12% of everything published, almost all in the legacy, gpt5 and preserved groups.

PRIVACY. 144 published offices share street and ZIP with the filing address of a donor who works at that employer. None has a suite, at most 2 filers use the address, and the employer has at most 3 donors. From the street names, 77 look like private homes: 50 legacy, 10 v3, 1 v3 office, 15 manual, 1 preserved. 76 of the 77 are primaries, so each becomes the company's pin, and the donor-employment rows point to it.
- Another 67 published rows have a residential street suffix and no donor overlap. About 12 of them also look like homes (e.g. ADELPHI DATA INC 6713 WEMBERLY WAY).
- This goes against the project's own manual policy. Other manual rows drop home streets on purpose ('home-based street intentionally omitted', LINE G 'INVALID: residential'). Yet AGINS INTERIOR is published as verified although its own note says 'HQ at owner's Marin County residence'.

RECOMMENDATION. Keep publishing manual_override, the v3 sourced primaries and the v3 offices. Stop publishing the 32 preserved rows and the 24 gpt5/xai rows. Publish legacy unsourced search rows only when the office state is one of the donors' states (905 kept, 561 held back until the v3 refresh that _needs_ai already has queued). Add a build-time check that withholds a published street when it is an employee's own home filing address.

After that change, INVALID also stops the paid re-lookup, because _needs_ai skips manual_invalid.

- USG needs an employer-name split per sub_id in cleaning, not an address block.

- Too broad. By their own count about 67 of the 144 matches are real storefronts or plants whose owners file the business address.
- It would drop the whole employer address, because the loader needs a street.
- It would override the deliberate HSK CONSULTING home-office decision.
- The loader already gives self-employed employments the donor's own address by design, so the added exposure is the company pin and label, not a new address.
- Safer: emit a review list, or apply it only to AI-sourced rows. Blank the street only on the manual rows whose own notes say residence or resident agent (AGINS, 510 VENTURES), after the user confirms the policy.
